title: Display Variables and String Interpolation
learningObjectives: Combine text and values using string concatenation.
Use interpolated strings to embed expressions in text.
Apply format specifiers and alignment to interpolated values.
Use invariant formatting when exact output must be culture-independent.

understand.concept: Displaying variables means converting values to text and sending that text to an output destination such as the console. C# offers concatenation, interpolated strings and formatting APIs. Interpolation is usually the clearest choice for combining labels with values.
understand.whyItMatters: Programs need to communicate calculated values, status and results. Clear formatting makes output easier to read and helps learners compare actual output with expected output.
understand.analogy: Displaying a variable is like filling blanks in a report with current values. Interpolation keeps the sentence readable while inserting values where needed.
understand.analogyLimit: Formatting does not change the underlying value. A formatted number is text for presentation; calculations should continue to use numeric types.

explain.narrative:
## Console output

Console.WriteLine writes a value followed by a line terminator. Overloads exist for common types; objects can be converted to text through their formatting behaviour.

## Concatenation

The plus operator can join strings. When one operand is a string, other values are converted to text, but long concatenation expressions can become difficult to maintain.

## String interpolation

Prefix a string literal with a dollar sign and place expressions inside braces. Interpolation supports format specifiers such as F2 for two decimal places and alignment components.

## Culture-aware formatting

Numeric formatting can vary by current culture. When exact output is required, use CultureInfo.InvariantCulture with ToString or string.Format. This makes examples reproducible across machines.

## Version baseline

String interpolation is supported from C# 6 onward. All examples are compatible with C# 14 and .NET 10.
